record.narrative: This first batch of 12 hypotheses tests main effects of three balanced binary predictors (feature_002, feature_034, feature_060) on four dependency outcomes selected for larger dispersion and sufficiently negative baseline means (outcome_001, outcome_008, outcome_011, outcome_013). The expected raw contrast is negative for exposed vs comparator because more negative dependency scores indicate stronger CRISPR dependency; I hypothesize that exposure=1 marks a biology associated with greater dependency. The clinically meaningful threshold is treated as at least about 10% relative difference versus the outcome-specific mean absolute score, e.g. outcome_001 ~0.0415, outcome_011 ~0.0301, outcome_013 ~0.0269, outcome_008 ~0.0282. Alternative hypotheses are no association or exposure associated with weaker dependency (less negative scores). These are initial discovery comparisons, not causal claims; follow-up will expand to other outcomes, categorical predictors, high-prevalence binary markers, continuous/thresholded predictors, and interactions only if signals are promising.

Run the full first discovery batch: main effects of feature_002, feature_034, and feature_060 on outcome_001, outcome_008, outcome_011, and outcome_013. These are balanced binary exposures, so all comparison cells should satisfy the minimum 20 observations. I selected these claims to screen for clinically meaningful negative dependency shifts: signed estimates are expected to be positive under the pre-registered direction if exposure is associated with more negative scores. The results will identify which predictor, if any, is worth broadening across the remaining outcomes and which should be deferred or closed.

The first discovery screen did not produce any clinically meaningful positive association in the preregistered direction. For the four outcomes tested, the 10% relative-difference thresholds based on outcome absolute means were approximately 0.0415 for outcome_001, 0.0301 for outcome_011, 0.0269 for outcome_013, and 0.0282 for outcome_008. All signed point estimates were either near zero (about 0.002-0.015) or negative (H2 and H7), well below the clinical threshold, and the 95% Welch intervals all crossed zero. Some intervals have upper bounds slightly above threshold, but none are supported by the point estimate and the evidence does not justify validating these exact comparisons. Cell sizes are ample, so the failure is not due to the minimum-count constraint. I reject these exact main-effect claims as unsupported in this dataset and close them, not as proof that these predictors cannot have subgroup or interaction effects elsewhere. The next scientific priority is to broaden the predictor search across other measured variables and outcomes, including categorical contrasts with adequate cell sizes and thresholded continuous predictors, rather than spending validation resources on these weak main effects.

No new validation evidence was delivered in this synthesis step. The first discovery batch remains negative for the exact comparisons registered: feature_002, feature_034, and feature_060 did not show clinically meaningful negative dependency-score shifts in outcome_001, outcome_008, outcome_011, or outcome_013. All point estimates were small relative to the 10% absolute-mean thresholds and all intervals crossed zero, so the evidence in this dataset does not support accepting those main effects. This does not establish causal nullity or rule out subgroup/interaction effects; it supports closing those specific comparisons as unsupported here. The next priority is to broaden the predictor search to different predictor classes and higher-variance outcomes rather than validating weak main effects. I therefore registered comparisons for a two-level categorical marker (feature_054, minority level_002 versus reference level_001), a moderate-prevalence binary marker (feature_045, present versus absent), and the absence of a high-prevalence binary marker (feature_008, 0 versus 1) across outcome_001, outcome_006, outcome_011, and outcome_014. The preregistered direction is negative because a lower dependency score means stronger dependency, while the anticipated raw contrast is left uncertain because predictor labels are opaque and their biological directions are not known in advance. These are discovery associations in the supplied dataset, not causal claims.

The active queue already contains 12 discovery claims for feature_054 level_002 vs level_001, feature_045 present vs absent, and feature_008 absent vs present. To reduce dependence on those three predictors and broaden discovery, I registered 12 additional main-effect comparisons using known adequate binary cell sizes. feature_047 tests absence of a high-prevalence marker (exposed 0, comparator 1; roughly 383 exposed and 1617 comparator), feature_021 tests presence of a lower-prevalence marker (roughly 406 exposed and 1594 comparator), and feature_032 tests a rare positive marker (roughly 110 exposed and 1890 comparator). All four outcomes remain outcome_001, outcome_006, outcome_011, and outcome_014 because these have sufficient variance and clinically interpretable absolute means. The preregistered direction is negative: if exposure marks stronger CRISPR dependency, the exposed-minus-comparator raw dependency-score difference should be more negative. Anticipated raw directions are left uncertain because predictor labels and biology are opaque. Alternatives are no association or exposure associated with weaker dependency, i.e., less negative scores. These are discovery associations in the supplied dataset, not causal claims; the key acceptance criterion is whether the signed mean difference is compatible with at least about 10% of the outcome-specific absolute mean.

No claims are due for assessment, and I do not request validation from existing evidence because the closed H1-H12 results are flat and not worth independent confirmation. For this analyze stage, I selected the next discovery tests to maximize predictor breadth rather than fully testing only the first three registered predictors. The 12 selected claims cover six candidate predictors: feature_054, feature_045, feature_008, feature_047, feature_021, and feature_032. Each predictor is screened on two outcomes: outcome_011 and outcome_014. Outcome_011 has a moderate clinical threshold and lower dispersion than some high-variance outcomes, whereas outcome_014 has a much smaller absolute mean and therefore a smaller 10% absolute threshold. These outcomes provide a reasonable first screen for whether any of the six predictors has a dependency-score association large enough to matter clinically. The remaining untested outcome claims for these predictors are deferred until follow-up: if a predictor shows a clinically meaningful or promising negative association on either screened outcome, I will expand that predictor across the other outcomes; if all selected screens are flat, I can then use the remaining queued claims to test alternative outcomes.

The second discovery batch screened six predictors on outcome_011 and outcome_014. Using signed evidence, positive estimates indicate that the exposed group has more negative dependency scores, i.e., stronger CRISPR dependency, which is the hypothesized meaningful direction. The approximate 10% absolute-mean thresholds were 0.0301 for outcome_011 and 0.0093 for outcome_014. Most screened comparisons were small, had intervals crossing zero, and did not support a clinically meaningful negative dependency-score shift. These include feature_054, feature_045, feature_008, feature_047, and feature_021; I reject those exact main-effect claims and close them, while acknowledging that subgroup or outcome-specific effects are not ruled out. Feature_032=1 versus 0 is the only promising predictor. On outcome_011 (H35/R23), the signed point estimate is +0.0351, slightly above threshold, but the interval [-0.0225, +0.0928] crosses zero and is wide; this is unresolved but deferred. On outcome_014 (H36/R24), the signed point estimate is +0.0685, far above the small outcome_014 threshold of 0.0093, and the interval [-0.0012, +0.1381] barely includes zero. This is clinically promising but imprecise, based on only 110 exposed observations, and one of 12 new screens, so I do not accept it on discovery evidence alone. I request independent validation for H36 to determine whether the feature_032 association with stronger outcome_014 dependency is robust.

The independent validation for H36 did not confirm the discovery result. For H36, feature_032=1 versus 0 and outcome_014, the signed discovery estimate was +0.0685, above the outcome_014 10% absolute-mean threshold of about 0.0093, but its discovery interval crossed zero and the exposed cell was only n=110. The independent validation estimate was -0.0114, i.e., in the opposite hypothesized direction, with a wide independent interval [-0.1001, 0.0772] at a stringent alpha level. Thus the validation is neither clinically supportive nor consistent with the discovery screen. The combined evidence does not support a robust clinically meaningful association between feature_032 and stronger outcome_014 dependency in this dataset, so I reject and close the exact H36 comparison. This rejection is limited to this measured predictor, outcome, and population; it does not prove causal nullity or exclude outcome-specific, thresholded, or subgroup effects. I do not treat the inverse validation point as evidence for a clinically meaningful reverse association because it is imprecise and inconsistent with discovery. H35 remains the unresolved feature_032/outcome_011 screen, but it is lower priority. To continue predictor discovery, I registered twelve new main-effect comparisons using six additional binary predictors with adequate cell sizes: feature_042, feature_020, feature_065, and feature_052 present versus absent, and feature_023 and feature_030 absent versus present. These were screened on outcome_014 and outcome_006 because their clinical thresholds are relatively small in absolute score units (about 0.0093 and 0.0175), making 10% relative differences easier to detect without accepting larger absolute thresholds. All exposed cells should exceed 20: feature_042 n1 about 463, feature_020 n1 about 343, feature_065 n1 about 401, feature_052 n1 about 381, feature_023 n0 about 235, and feature_030 n0 about 207. The preregistered direction remains negative for dependency scores, so a positive signed estimate indicates stronger dependency in the exposed group. Anticipated raw directions are left uncertain because predictor labels and biology are opaque.

There are no assessment deadlines. After the feature_032/outcome_014 screen failed independent validation, I am shifting away from one-off low-prevalence binary markers and toward a wider set of predictors that can be tested with adequate and more transparent cell sizes. This proposal batch adds four untested binary markers and several contrasts within a four-level categorical predictor. The binary markers are feature_012, feature_050, feature_022, and feature_001. Their positive-cell sizes are approximately 376, 412, 254, and 130, respectively, so each comparison cell is well above the minimum of 20. For the categorical predictor, I chose feature_055 because its most frequent level has n=519 and there are four levels; given the reported top frequency, the remaining levels together have n=1481, making each contrast with a non-top level expected to be adequately powered and cell-safe. I compare non-top levels to level_003, the reported top level, because that gives a coherent reference-group framing across nominal levels. The outcomes include outcome_011, outcome_014, outcome_006, and outcome_001. Outcome_011 has a relatively favorable threshold-to-dispersion profile (10% absolute-mean threshold about 0.0301), while outcome_014 and outcome_006 have smaller absolute-mean thresholds but larger residual variance, so they may reveal clinically meaningful effects with more caution. Outcome_001 is included to broaden outcome coverage despite a larger threshold (about 0.0415). The preregistered direction is negative in dependency-score units, meaning the exposed level or marker is hypothesized to be associated with stronger CRISPR dependency, i.e., more negative scores. Anticipated raw directions are left uncertain because predictor labels are opaque and no main effect was robustly established earlier. Plausible alternatives are no association, an association in the weaker-dependency direction, or an effect confined to a single outcome or nominal level. These are discovery associations in the supplied dataset, not causal claims.

No claims are currently due for assessment, so this analyze stage requests the next discovery tests without validation. I selected the newly registered H49-H60 batch because it adds several adequate-cell binary markers and a four-level categorical predictor, and it includes outcome_011, which has a more favorable threshold-to-dispersion profile than the very noisy small-mean outcomes used in previous binary screens. The binary predictors feature_012, feature_050, feature_022, and feature_001 have exposed cell sizes around 376, 412, 254, and 130, respectively, all above the minimum-cell requirement. The categorical predictor feature_055 is also scientifically attractive: it has four nominal levels with the most frequent level containing 519 observations, implying that level contrasts against the modal level are likely well powered and cell-safe. Across these claims, signed positive estimates still denote the hypothesized meaningful direction, i.e., stronger CRISPR dependency in the exposed group or exposed categorical level. This batch is intended to reduce reliance on the earlier feature_032 signal that failed independent validation and to test whether any higher-prevalence binary or categorical predictor shows a clinically meaningful association. H37-H48 remain queued for follow-up if this batch is flat or if predictor-specific patterns motivate broader outcome screening.

This batch screens feature_012, feature_050, feature_022, feature_001, and feature_055 nominal contrasts using outcome_011, outcome_014, outcome_006, and outcome_001. Because all claims use direction -1, signed positive estimates denote the hypothesized biologically meaningful direction: stronger CRISPR dependency in the exposed group or exposed categorical level. Approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0301 for outcome_011, 0.0093 for outcome_014, 0.0175 for outcome_006, and 0.0415 for outcome_001. Most results are near null, have intervals crossing zero, and do not provide interval support for a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency effect. H49, H51, H53, H55, H57, and H58 have signed estimates well below their outcome thresholds or in the opposite direction; H50, H54, and H59 are either opposite-direction or imprecisely below/around threshold and do not support the original stronger-dependency hypothesis; H60 is small and imprecise. Therefore I reject and close those exact comparisons in this dataset, while noting that rejection does not exclude thresholded, subgroup, interaction, or outcome-specific effects. Two comparisons are only marginally clinically interesting: H52, feature_050=1 versus 0 on outcome_014, signed +0.0122 with interval [-0.0266, +0.0511], and H56, feature_001=1 versus 0 on outcome_014, signed +0.0141 with interval [-0.0507, +0.0788]. Their point estimates exceed the small outcome_014 threshold, but the intervals are wide, include zero and opposite-direction values, and do not establish a clinically meaningful association. H56 is less trustworthy because the exposed cell has only 130 observations, while H52 has better cell balance but remains imprecise. Given the failure of H36 independent validation despite a stronger point estimate, and the large number of discovery screens, I do not accept or validate these now. I defer H52 and H56 as fragile candidate signals. I do not request independent validation because no new result has a confidence interval near the clinical threshold or enough stability to justify spending validation capacity; validation is better reserved for a signal with a clearer interval and/or replicated discovery evidence.

The independent validation result for H1 strengthens the original rejection. For feature_002=1 versus 0 on outcome_001, the signed validation estimate is +0.0048, with interval [-0.0428, 0.0524]. A signed positive value would indicate stronger CRISPR dependency in the exposed group, but the point estimate is far below the approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical threshold for outcome_001 (~0.0415) and the interval is centered near zero, crossing both null and clinically important values. The discovery result R1 was similarly small (+0.0061; interval [-0.0260, 0.0383]). Together, these data provide no support for a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency association for this exact contrast, and they also do not support a clinically meaningful reverse association. I therefore keep H1 rejected and closed. This rejection is limited to this measured predictor, outcome, and population, and does not exclude associations of feature_002 with other outcomes, thresholded predictors, or subgroup effects. Overall, the accepted claim set remains empty. The study now has a substantial set of negative main-effect results for common binary predictors and selected outcome screens, especially on outcome_001, outcome_011, outcome_013, outcome_008, outcome_006, and outcome_014. A few unresolved or deferred signals remain: H35 feature_032 with outcome_011, H52 feature_050 with outcome_014, and H56 feature_001 with outcome_014. Their discovery point estimates can exceed the outcome-specific 10% thresholds, but intervals are wide and include clinically null values, and one closely related feature_032 signal failed independent validation. Therefore, I do not treat these as supported clinically meaningful associations. The next analysis should complete the queued H37-H48 main-effect screen, then pursue a small, prespecified interaction screen. The new interaction proposals focus on high-prevalence binary predictors feature_002, feature_034, and feature_060, and on a continuous thresholded contrast feature_010>=0 versus <0, measured on outcome_011 and outcome_008. These are scientifically informative because they test whether context-specific associations exist even when main effects are null. The one targeted refinement linked to H52 asks whether the feature_050 outcome_014 signal is concentrated in the feature_042 subgroup. If these interaction screens are also flat, the most informative conclusion in this dataset is that the tested measured predictors do not show robust, clinically meaningful associations with stronger CRISPR dependency across the examined outcomes, while broader modeling of predictor classes, interactions, or subgroups remains a necessary follow-up. All conclusions remain observational associations within the supplied dataset, not causal effects or generalizable claims.

No claims are due for assessment, so the explore action is to redirect the next discovery wave toward outcomes with better signal-to-noise and predictors with adequate cell sizes. Prior screens have not produced accepted claims: feature_002 on outcome_001 was rejected after both discovery and independent validation were near null, feature_032 on outcome_014 failed validation despite a larger discovery point estimate, and many binary and categorical main-effect contrasts have been near null or imprecise. Some earlier follow-up screens used outcome_014 and outcome_006, which have small absolute 10% mean thresholds but very large residual variance, making clinically meaningful associations harder to confirm. The current proposals therefore move to outcome_002 and outcome_015. Their approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0260 and 0.0250, with SDs about 0.1757 and 0.1746, giving a more favorable detectability profile than outcome_014 or outcome_006. These outcomes also remain completely untested in the existing accepted/unresolved evidence, so they broaden outcome coverage rather than repeatedly probing noisy endpoints.

The proposed predictors are chosen to avoid low-prevalence instability and to test whether any high- or moderate-prevalence binary predictor has outcome-specific associations that were missed on earlier endpoints. The high-prevalence predictors feature_002, feature_034, and feature_060 have exposed cell sizes near 989, 1039, and 996 in the full population, respectively. The newly introduced moderate-prevalence predictors feature_037, feature_027, and feature_011 have estimated positive-cell sizes about 411, 393, and 310, respectively, comfortably above the minimum-cell requirement. All comparisons are preregistered with direction -1, meaning a signed positive estimate indicates stronger CRISPR dependency, i.e. a more negative dependency score, in the exposed group. Anticipated raw directions remain uncertain because the predictor labels and biological roles are opaque and no predictor has yet produced robust clinically meaningful main effects. Plausible alternatives include: no association, an association in the weaker-dependency direction, an association confined to one outcome, or an effect only after interaction/subgroup restriction. These are observational discovery associations within the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims. If this outcome_002/outcome_015 screen is flat together with the queued H37-H48 binary screens, the most defensible interim conclusion will be that the tested measured binary predictors do not show robust clinically meaningful main effects across the examined CRISPR dependency score family. The next scientific focus would then be context-specific hypotheses, continuous-threshold or interaction analyses, or broader modeling rather than another round of marginal low-prevalence binary screens.

No claims are due for assessment, so this analyze stage requests the next discovery analyses without validation. I selected the full newly registered H67-H78 batch because it tests six binary predictors on outcome_002 and outcome_015, the two most favorable untested outcomes among those with stable dispersion: approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0260 for outcome_002 and 0.0250 for outcome_015, with SDs around 0.176 and 0.175, respectively. This batch includes high-prevalence predictors feature_002, feature_034, and feature_060 as well as moderate-prevalence feature_037, feature_027, and feature_011, all with adequate exposed-cell sizes. Compared with the queued H37-H48 main-effect screens, which are focused on noisy small-mean outcomes outcome_014 and outcome_006, these new analyses are more likely to produce interpretable evidence about clinically meaningful associations. H61-H66 interactions and the remaining H37-H48 comparisons remain available for follow-up depending on whether this stable-outcome screen reveals directionally coherent signals.

This batch tests six binary predictors on outcome_002 and outcome_015. With direction -1, signed positive estimates mean stronger CRISPR dependency in the exposed group. Approximate absolute-mean 10% clinical thresholds are 0.0260 for outcome_002 and 0.0250 for outcome_015. Most results are near null, cross zero, or have point estimates far below the clinical threshold, and the entire positive interval often remains below the 10% magnitude. I therefore reject and close H67-H69 and H71-H75 and H77-H78 as exact comparisons in this dataset. These rejections do not exclude subgroup, interaction, thresholded, or other outcome-specific effects.

Two comparisons are borderline candidates. H70, feature_034=1 versus 0 on outcome_015, has signed estimate +0.0170, interval [0.0017, 0.0323], corresponding to about 6.8% of the absolute outcome mean. It is the only comparison in this batch with a 95% discovery interval excluding zero, but the point estimate is still below the 10% clinical threshold, although the interval includes clinically meaningful positive values. Because it is a well-powered contrast with good cell sizes and the most defensible signal among the twelve tests, I keep it unresolved and request independent validation. The prior false-positive/validation failure in this run makes validation appropriate here, especially given the multiplicity of the twelve-test screen. I do not accept it yet because the discovery point estimate does not meet the clinically meaningful magnitude and one nominal result among many could be noise.

H76, feature_027=1 versus 0 on outcome_015, has signed estimate +0.0177, interval [-0.0016, 0.0369], also about 7.1% of the absolute outcome mean. It is suggestive but weaker because the interval crosses zero by a small amount and its point estimate is below threshold. I defer it rather than validating it, because H70 is the stronger candidate and validation capacity should be reserved. The remaining comparisons are either opposite direction, null, or imprecise and not clinically meaningful. These are observational associations within the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

H36 response deadline: feature_032=1 versus 0 on outcome_014 had a nominally promising discovery estimate (+0.0685; interval [-0.0012, 0.1381]) that exceeded the approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical threshold for outcome_014 (~0.0093), but independent validation is near null and opposite in signed direction (-0.0114; independent interval [-0.1001, 0.0772]). The validation interval is wide, crosses zero, and includes large positive and negative values, but it fails to reproduce the discovery point and provides no support for a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency association. I therefore keep H36 rejected and closed. This rejection is specific to this predictor-outcome main-effect contrast in the supplied dataset; it does not exclude feature_032 effects on other outcomes, low-prevalence H35, or context-dependent effects.

H70 independent validation: feature_034=1 versus 0 on outcome_015 had discovery evidence +0.0170 (interval [0.0017, 0.0323]), roughly 6.8% of the absolute outcome mean, below the approximate 10% clinical threshold (~0.0250) but with an upper bound that entered clinically meaningful territory. The independent validation is much smaller: +0.0029 (interval [-0.0205, 0.0263]), about 1.2% of the absolute mean. The validation point is near zero, the interval crosses null and negative values, and although its upper bound is marginally above threshold, it is not centered on or supportive of a clinically meaningful effect. Across discovery and validation, there is no robust evidence that feature_034=1 versus 0 is associated with a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency effect on outcome_015. I therefore reject and close H70 as an exact main-effect claim. I reactivate H76 rather than close it: it is the only remaining candidate from the outcome_002/outcome_015 binary screen (feature_027 on outcome_015: +0.0177, interval [-0.0016, 0.0369]); its point estimate is below threshold and the interval crosses zero, so it remains unresolved and should be considered only as a low-confidence candidate, not an accepted finding.

Overall synthesis: no claims are supported by accepted evidence. The accepted claim set remains empty. The study now has a large set of negative or non-confirmatory exact main-effect comparisons across several CRISPR dependency score outcomes. High-prevalence binary predictors feature_002, feature_034, and feature_060 do not show robust clinically meaningful stronger-dependency associations on the outcomes where they have been adequately tested. Low-prevalence or noisy candidate signals (H35, H52, H56, and H76) remain unresolved but are not supported; H36 and H70 failed independent validation, increasing caution about nominal discovery signals. Unresolved uncertainty also includes many untested outcomes and predictor classes, interactions, and thresholded/subgroup effects. The most informative next analyses are conditional and context-specific: evaluate registered interaction claims H61-H66 plus targeted refinements testing whether feature_034 or feature_027 associations on outcome_015 are concentrated in feature_010>=0 versus <0. A small broad screen of feature_002, feature_034, feature_060, and feature_027 on outcome_012 can improve coverage of stable untested dependency-score outcomes. Main-effect screens on noisy small-mean outcomes outcome_014/outcome_006 remain lower priority unless an interaction or multi-outcome coherence provides a lead. Future validation should be reserved for comparisons whose discovery interval itself points to clinically meaningful magnitude or shows coherent replication across related outcomes. All conclusions remain observational associations within the supplied dataset, not causal effects or generalizable biological claims.

No claims are due for assessment. The next wave is intentionally structured around the only remaining suggestive candidate, H76 feature_027=1 versus 0 on outcome_015 (signed estimate +0.0177, interval [-0.0016, 0.0369]), while preserving broad exploration. The approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical threshold for outcome_015 is about 0.0250, so H76 is below the magnitude required for acceptance and remains only a low-confidence candidate. The new linked refinements test whether this signal is concentrated in a higher feature_010 context, replicated across related stable dependency-score outcomes, or modified by another high-prevalence binary predictor. With direction -1, a signed positive estimate corresponds to stronger CRISPR dependency in the exposed group. The feature_010>=0 and feature_010>=1 conditional contrasts test whether the association is concentrated in the broad and more extreme high-context regions. If both remain near null, the concentrated-context explanation for H76 is disfavored. If they become clinically meaningful, that would justify further replication or validation rather than immediate acceptance, because they are context-specific follow-ups of an already unresolved signal. The outcome_005, outcome_016, and outcome_007 feature_027 contrasts test multi-outcome coherence; directionally consistent estimates near or above the roughly 0.025 thresholds would strengthen the candidate, whereas null or opposite estimates make H76 more plausibly outcome-specific noise or a very weak association. The feature_027-by-feature_060 interaction tests whether the population effect is masked by opposite or absent effects outside a feature_060=1 context. In addition, the unlinked proposals broaden coverage of high-prevalence and categorical predictors on stable outcomes outcome_005 and outcome_016: feature_034 on these outcomes, feature_054 level_002 versus level_001, and feature_055 level_004 versus level_003. These keep the investigation from becoming overfit to one predictor and test predictor classes that have not been screened on these outcomes. All proposals remain observational associations in the supplied dataset; acceptance will require effect magnitude near or above the outcome-specific 10% threshold, interval support, and, where needed, coherence or validation rather than a single nominal result.

No claims are due for assessment, so this analyze stage requests discovery analyses without validation. I selected 12 untested comparisons that most directly address the only remaining suggestive candidate, H76 feature_027=1 versus 0 on outcome_015 (signed +0.0177 [-0.0016, 0.0369]), while still adding broad stable-outcome coverage. H85 and H86 test whether the feature_027 signal is concentrated in higher feature_010 contexts. H87, H88, H89, and H84 test coherence across related stable dependency-score outcomes outcome_005, outcome_016, outcome_007, and outcome_012; their approximate absolute-mean 10% clinical thresholds are about 0.0250, 0.0256, 0.0245, and 0.0248, respectively. With direction -1, positive signed estimates indicate stronger CRISPR dependency in the feature_027=1 group. H96 tests whether the feature_027 main effect is modified by feature_060=1 versus feature_060=0. If feature_027 remains only a borderline outcome_015 finding and these conditional, cross-outcome, or interaction analyses are null or opposite, the exact main-effect candidate becomes much less defensible. The remaining selected comparisons, H90-H94, broaden screening of high-prevalence binary feature_034 and categorical predictors feature_054 and feature_055 on stable outcomes outcome_005 and outcome_016, except that H95 is omitted to preserve slot capacity for outcome_012 coherence. These analyses are observational discovery tests within the supplied dataset; future conclusions about causal direction or generalizability will require independent evidence beyond these comparisons.

With direction -1, positive signed estimates indicate stronger CRISPR dependency in the exposed group. The approximate outcome_015 clinical threshold is about 0.0250. H86, feature_027=1 versus 0 within feature_010>=1 on outcome_015, is the only new result whose point estimate exceeds threshold: +0.0447, roughly 17.9% of the absolute outcome mean. However, its cell sizes are small and imbalanced (exposed 56, comparator 278), and the interval is very wide and crosses null: [-0.0111, 0.1004]. Because the discovery interval does not provide uncertainty support and this is one comparison among many, I do not accept it. I keep H86 unresolved and active but do not request validation: the small exposed cell and wide interval make independent validation likely inconclusive, and prior false-positive/validation failures warrant reserving validation for signals whose discovery interval itself points more clearly to clinically meaningful magnitude.

H85, feature_010>=0, is weaker and less precise than the overall H76 result, with estimate +0.0156 [-0.0134, 0.0447], below threshold and crossing zero; reject and close. Cross-outcome coherence is poor: H87 outcome_005 gives opposite direction (-0.0172), H88 outcome_016 is near null (-0.0044), H89 outcome_007 is opposite (-0.0150), and H84 outcome_012 is null (+0.0033). H96 feature_027-by-feature_060 interaction is null (+0.0144 [-0.0242, 0.0531]). Taken together, these make H76 feature_027=1 versus 0 on outcome_015 unlikely to be a robust clinically meaningful main effect, so I reassess H76 as rejected and closed based on its own borderline estimate plus these non-coherent follow-up contrasts.

The other screens are not clinically meaningful. H90 feature_034 outcome_005 is positive but only +0.0102 and crosses zero; H91 feature_034 outcome_016 is opposite; H92/H93 feature_054 are null; H94 feature_055 outcome_005 is null/opposite. I reject and close these exact comparisons. The next step is targeted testing of the sole H86 context signal: whether feature_027 has a genuine feature_010>=1 interaction versus its complement, and whether the same context replicates on outcome_005, outcome_016, and outcome_007. If those remain inconsistent or imprecise, H86 should be closed. All conclusions remain observational associations in the supplied dataset.

H1 independent validation closes the exact feature_002 versus feature_002 main-effect claim on outcome_001. With direction -1, discovery signed estimate +0.0061, interval [-0.0260,0.0383], and validation signed estimate +0.0048, interval [-0.0428,0.0524]. Both are near null relative to the approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical threshold of about 0.0415. The validation interval is wide because of the independent correction, but the point estimate is tiny and does not reproduce a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency signal; therefore H1 remains rejected and closed. This is a dataset-specific negative result for this predictor-outcome contrast, not a claim of universal absence. Overall supported findings: none. The accepted claim set remains empty. The study now contains many negative exact main-effect or validated negative results across high-prevalence binary predictors and several dependency-score outcomes. Validation failures for feature_032/outcome_014 and feature_034/outcome_015 further caution against accepting nominal discovery signals whose point estimates are below or only barely above the 10% threshold. Unresolved uncertainty: H86, feature_027=1 versus 0 on outcome_015 within feature_010>=1, remains active. Its signed estimate is +0.0447, above the approximate outcome_015 threshold of 0.0250, but the interval [-0.0111,0.1004] is wide, includes null and subclinical values, and the exposed cell is only 56. The prior coherence failures around the broader feature_027/outcome_015 signal mean H86 should be treated as a context-specific hypothesis, not an accepted finding. The most informative next analysis is the focused active set: H86 plus H97 interaction and H98-H100 conditional coherence for feature_027 in feature_010>=1, H81-H83 stable outcome_012 screens, H95 outcome_016 feature_055 level_004 versus level_003, and the newly registered outcome_005/016/007 feature_027-by-feature_010 interactions. If these context contrasts are consistently positive, centered near or above the relevant 10% thresholds, and interval-supported away from null, then validation becomes more justified.
